records.before_content: More evidence for the add_memory entities-gate false-conflict bug (owner task 6059), seen 2026-10-01 during a /reflect. Four of eight writes were rejected with DeclaredReferentConflictRejected when the content referred to tasks by bare number ("5303", "landed with 5303", "Residual of 5303") while entities declared {'kind':'task','id':5303}. The content scanner recognised only the "Task NNNN" / "task NNNN" spellings as referents, and in one case mis-extracted 'tip:23313' (a test count) and 'filed:6155' as referents. As a result, every declared task counted as a conflict. Workaround: omit entities; the write then succeeds and the scanner derives referents. Writing "task 5303" (with the word) also makes the scanner see the referent.
records.rationale: Named by task 7117. "Workaround: omit entities; the write then succeeds".

records.before_content: Hand-carry mechanics that worked on 2026-10-05 (task 5344 via carrier task 6377): (a) implement in an out-of-tree worktree (.claude/worktrees/hc-<id>), and when review fixes arrive while a full test_command run is still going in that tree, branch a SECOND worktree from the rebased tip for the fixer instead of editing under the running suite; (b) file the carrier up front with submit_task(planning_mode=True) + add_dependency(carrier -> real task) while the real task is held deferred; at submit time `git branch task/<carrier> <tip>` + `git worktree add .worktrees/<carrier>` (no git worktree move, so no broken venv), walk carrier pending -> in-progress (claimant_run_id) -> merge-deferred, submit with verified_green only if the suite ran on that exact tip; (c) the queue was 9 deep: the carrier was coalesced as a NON-TIP train member (superseded_by coalesce-5479-*), the train landed ~3h after submit under the tip's marker, and mark_member_done flipped the merge-deferred carrier to done ~1 min after the marker appeared (no self-stamp needed or allowed); the real task (deferred) was stamped done with found_on_main at its landed rebased commit, proven by `git cherry main task/<carrier>` all '-'. A Bash safety check refused `bash -c "$TC"` (it cannot inspect a variable script for rm); writing the verbatim test_command into a visible script file worked. The fused-memory entities gate rejected declared tasks cited as bare numbers ('carrier 6377', '5371 and 5020') as conflicts; write 'task N' each time or omit entities.
records.rationale: Found by the literal sweep only. Ends "write 'task N' each time or omit entities".

records.before_content: add_memory's entities check (declared_referent_conflict) recognises a task referent in the content only in the form 'task NNNN' (or 'Task NNNN'). records.before_content:
add_memory's entities declaration is checked against referents the content scanner derives, and the scanner reads only some id forms. On 2026-10-09 a decisions_and_rationale write listing many bare task numbers ('α 6667, β 6668 …') declared those tasks in `entities` and was rejected with DeclaredReferentConflictRejected. The scanner had derived only 'Task 6673', 'reify:8430' and 'amendments:6106' from the prose, so every other declared id counted as a conflict. Retrying with `entities` omitted succeeded.
Rule of thumb: for a memory naming many ids in compact notation, omit `entities`, or rephrase each id as 'task NNNN'.
records.rationale: Named by task 7117. Rule of thumb "omit `entities`" for many compact ids.

records.before_content:
add_memory writing lesson (2026-10-02): the entities gate rejects bare ids in a write about a batch.

What happened: a session-summary write that referred to tasks as "α 6181" or "(6184)" while declaring them in `entities` was rejected with DeclaredReferentConflictRejected. The content scan recognises only the spelling "task NNNN", so a bare id or a Greek-label id reads as undeclared. This is the false-conflict class root-caused 2026-09-28, owner task 6059.

Fix that worked: spell every referent "task NNNN" in the text (e.g. "α = task 6181"), so the declaration matches. Keep `entities` rather than dropping it.

Separate pitfall, the completion-claim gate (info-level L0 escalations esc-unverified-claim-*):
- it flags "Task N filed …" as a filing_dispatch claim when N is `pending`;
- it flags a spec sentence such as "Task N reads X" as an applied_work claim.
Both are false positives. Close them with resolve_issue(action='close_only') and a stated reason. Prefer phrasing like "task N will read" or "task N is specified to read".

records.before_content: Convention (task 3675): every in-repo site that teaches add_memory/add_episode referent declaration is certified by fused-memory/tests/test_referent_declaration_examples.py. Its _GUARDED_SITES tuple lists them. Each `entities=<list literal>` is EXECUTED against the live entities_gate together with the content= string of its own call. The extractor fails loudly on placeholders (`entities=[<id>]`), on non-literals, and on prose `entities=` with no list after it, so write "omit `entities`" without the "=". Every guarded site must show at least one NON-EMPTY declaration whose content names the task it declares, because [] alone teaches nothing about the entry shape. A new site is one more _GUARDED_SITES entry: import Python constants, never regex their source. If it is a skills/ file, also register it in SKILLS_CONSUMING_TESTS and in the dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml enumeration. The recon prompts get the text from fused_memory.utils.referent_resolution::render_referent_declaration_guidance, which composes _DECLARED_REFERENT_HINT. Do not restate the entry shape anywhere else.
records.rationale: Census record (reviewed_not_target there): its "omit `entities`" is about prose spelling for the example extractor.

records.before_content:
Completed: entities_gate: a declared referent the scanner cannot see is rejected as a conflict whenever any other task is scannable (false DeclaredReferentConflictRejected)
Description: PROBLEM. `add_memory(entities=[...])` rejects HONEST declarations with `DeclaredReferentConflictRejected` whenever the content spells one declared task in a form the label scanner cannot see while ALSO mentioning some other task in a form it can. Reproduced 2026-09-28 against the live code (group_id='reify', but the mechanism is project-independent):

| content | declared | scan sees | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Merged task-173-fillet-fix; closes the loop.` | 173 | nothing | accept |
| `Merged task-173-fillet-fix after task 170 landed.` | 173 | Task 170 | REJECT |
| `gate 184 passed; task 190 unblocked.` | 184, 190 | Task 190 | REJECT (184) |
| `branch task/173 merged; task 5 noted` | 173 | Task 5 | REJECT |
| `Tasks 5949/5849 ...` (dark_factory, 2026-09-28) | 5849 | Task 5949 | REJECT |

Live sightings: Mem0 memory 4214c151-8776-4efa-99dd-8a12f02906e1 (solar_challenge_platform, 2026-09-27: slug `task-173-liveness-investigation` + `gate 184`), and dark_factory memories 525ad930, d3d753ef, 454d5a87 (2026-09-21/28: `5811's`, `4237 and 5671`, `tasks 3659 and 3500`, `via carrier 6033`). 13 `entities_gate: rejecting` journal lines since 2026-09-01 fleet-wide; the split between genuine typo catches and this false class is unmeasured.

CAUSAL CHAIN (found by /team lead 2026-09-28, verified by direct reproduction):
1. `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/utils/canonical_labels.py::_LOCAL_MENTION_PATTERN` is precision-over-recall by design (PRD `plans/memory-referent-fidelity-prd.md` resolved decision 8). It matches `task` + whitespace/`#`/`:` + digits and `<project>:<digits>` only. Hyphen slugs (`task-173-foo`), branch names (`task/173`), possessives that the scanner happens to catch or not (`5811's`), slash lists (`5949/5849`), `and`-lists after a plural (`tasks 3659 and 3500`) and non-task vocabulary (`gate 184`, `carrier 6033`) are invisible. The slug and branch-name spellings are NOT on decision 8's published blind list, yet they are this fleet's own naming convention.
2. Both `referent_resolution.py` and `entities_gate.py` docstrings state the load-bearing rule: the scanner's SILENCE is uninformative and must never reject an honest write.
3. ROOT CAUSE: `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/utils/referent_resolution.py::_conflicting_referents` applies that rule PER KIND, not PER REFERENT (its docstring, "choice 4": "An EMPTY per-kind scan never conflicts"). A declared task conflicts iff the scan found ANY task of that kind and not this one. So silence about 173 is "uninformative" when the scan found nothing, but becomes "contradiction" the moment an unrelated Task 170 appears in the same prose — even though the scanner's inability to see 173 is identical in both cases. The typo-catch (`[3127, 3129]` against 'Task 3127') and the blind-spot tolerance collide in this mixed case, and the rule resolves every such case as "typo". `tests/test_referent_resolution.py::TestConflictsAreReportedNotEnforced::test_a_superset_conflicts_per_ref` pins the typo case; `test_the_scanners_blind_list_never_manufactures_a_conflict` pins only the EMPTY-scan blind case, so the mixed case was never exercised.
4. The design's own statement of purpose is inverted in exactly the case the parameter exists for: the `add_memory` docstring says a declaration "is how you correct a body whose prose names a task ambiguously or not at all", and the PRD makes declared > metadata > derived a strict precedence. Under the current rule the derived scan overrules the declaration.
5. On a Mem0-primary category (observations_and_summaries, procedural_knowledge, preferences_and_norms) the declaration is validated and then DISCARDED (docstring "scope note"), so on those writes the gate can only ever cost a false rejection and can never buy anything. The 4214c151 sighting was observations_and_summaries.
6. `entities_gate.py::_ENTITIES_CONFLICT_HINT` tells the agent to "drop `entities` entirely". Agents did, then recorded "omitting entities fixes it" as durable memories (the four ids above), which now teach every future agent to stop declaring — directly against PRD decision 4 (declaration rate is the tracked adoption signal; task 3676 is the tighten-or-hold census). For a Graphiti write, dropping the declaration also misattributes the memory: only the scannable task (170) is derived and the real subject (173) is lost.

DELIVERABLE (the fix; the corpus repair is a separate operational task filed alongside this one):
A. Change `_conflicting_referents` so that a declared referent the scan did not see is a conflict ONLY when the scan supplies positive evidence of a typo, not merely evidence that some other task exists. Recommended rule: conflict iff the scan found, for the same kind (and project, for a foreign declaration), a referent whose number is a NEAR-MISS of the declared one (single-digit substitution / transposition / one-digit insertion-deletion — the adjacent-number typo the PRD's `[3127, 3129]` example describes) AND the declared number itself is absent. A scanned number with no near-miss relation to the declared one is silence, not disagreement. Keep the project-axis conflict (`test_the_project_axis_conflicts`) as is. Record the chosen rule in the docstring beside choices 1-4 and update `test_a_superset_conflicts_per_ref` to say WHY 3129-vs-3127 still conflicts; add the mixed-case tests from the table above as accepts (including `task-173-foo … task 170`, `task/173 … task 5`, `Tasks 5949/5849`, `tasks 3659 and 3500`).
B. Skip the conflict check entirely for a write whose declaration will be discarded — Mem0-primary category with dual_write=False — OR make the declaration RECORDED on Mem0 writes so it is no longer discarded. Either resolves the "pure cost" asymmetry of step 5; pick the first unless the second is trivial, and say which in the task's done summary. Consider whether `add_episode` has the same asymmetry.
C. Teach `canonical_labels.py` the fleet's own spellings that decision 8 never listed: hyphen slug `task-173(-…)` and branch name `task/173`. Both are bounded, low-false-positive patterns (the `task` word is still required). Extend `_LOCAL_MENTION_PATTERN`'s separator alternation rather than adding a pattern (INV-5: one vocabulary site). `Tasks 5949/5849` / `tasks 3659 and 3500` list forms are OPTIONAL — only if a precision argument can be made in the same style as the existing per-clause measurements.
